newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: NURSES WAGE RISE BUDGETED FOR, SAYS NSW GOVT
In New South Wales, there's concern about how a new 14-percent wage rise for nurses will be funded.
The Nurses Association has been negotiating a new award with the government over the past six-months.
Under the changes, nurses will receive a 12-percent increase without trade-offs and a further two-percent for productivity improvements.
The Opposition wants to know where the money is coming from, but Health Minister Andrew Refshauge says it's been accounted for in the Budget.
The agreement's expected to be signed early next week.
MAN RELEASED FROM JAIL TODAY ON SUPREME COURT ORDER
One of the men convicted over the murder of Sydney woman Megan Kalajzich 20-years-ago, has been released from jail today on the order of the Supreme Court.
Kerry Neil Orrock was sentenced to life in jail in May 1988, after being found guilty with several others of murder and conspiracy to murder Mrs Kalajzich.
He applied to the Supreme Court for a determination of his life sentence and Justice David Hunt today set a minimum term of eight years and seven months, which concluded last month.
Justice Hunt ordered that Orrock be released from custody immediately.
Mrs Kalajzich's husband Andrew, convicted of hiring others to murder his wife, has also asked the court to determine his life sentence.
The decision has been reserved.
FOX STUDIOS SUBMIT APPLICATION
The 150-million dollar Fox Studio development at the Sydney Showground has moved a step closer.
Fox Studios have submitted development applications for the film studios.
They're due to take bookings from film studios next year.
New South Wales Premier Bob Carr says the developmenmt application permits Fox to restore every heritage building on the Showground site.
UNIONS WARN OF JOB LOSSES IN FINANCE INDUSTRY
Unions say up to 40-thousand banking jobs could go, under a plan to restructure the finance industry.
The Finance Sector Union says there'll be massive job losses if the federal government accepts an industry recommendation to allow bank amalgamations.
The union's Tony Beck has sounded the warning as the final public hearing for the Wallis inquiry into the finance sector, gets underway in Melbourne.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
